title: Reduced closed subspaces and their supports after base change
statement: Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space], schemes use [def-pc-scheme], and universes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Their point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over a scheme $S$, and let $T\subseteq|X|$ be closed. There is a unique reduced closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $|Z|=T$. Here a closed subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable and becomes a closed immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduced means that its etale scheme charts are reduced, that is, their local rings have no nonzero nilpotents. For every morphism of algebraic spaces $q:W\to X$, the projection $Z\times_XW\to W$ is a closed immersion and identifies its underlying point space homeomorphically with $|q|^{-1}(T)$. No reducedness is asserted for this base change.

source.place: Tag 03IQ (lemma-reduced-closed-subspace); support after base change: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), and spaces.tex Tag 02YW (lemma-base-change-immersions).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], $R=U\times_XU$ is a scheme and its projections $s,t$ are surjective etale. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|p|$ is continuous and surjective, so $T_U=|p|^{-1}T$ is closed. Since $ps=pt$, the subsets $|s|^{-1}T_U$ and $|t|^{-1}T_U$ of $|R|$ coincide.

By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], let $D\hookrightarrow U$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $T_U$. The scheme pullbacks $D_s=R\times_{s,U}D$ and $D_t=R\times_{t,U}D$ are closed in $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Their projections to $D$ are etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], so both schemes are reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. Their point images in $R$ are $|s|^{-1}T_U$ and $|t|^{-1}T_U$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Step 1 makes these equal. The uniqueness clause of the reduced induced closed-subscheme theorem therefore identifies $D_s=D_t$ as closed subschemes of $R$. This is scheme-theoretic invariance, not merely equality of supports.

source.place: Tag 03IQ, middle of proof; reducedness without Noetherian hypotheses is justified by descent.tex Tag 034E (lemma-reduced-local-smooth).

proof.text: Regard $X$ as the discrete fibred groupoid of its sheaf of sets. It is an etale stack: compatible objects glue by the sheaf axiom, and all arrows are identities. Its diagonal is representable and $U\to X$ is an atlas by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every scheme test of this atlas is surjective etale, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; thus it is an algebraic stack as defined in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-closed-substack-descent] to the invariant $D\subset U$. It gives a closed substack $\mathcal Z\subset X$ with $U\times_X\mathcal Z=D$. Since it is strictly full in the discrete $X$, $\mathcal Z$ is exactly a set subfunctor $F\subset X$; its etale-stack gluing is the etale sheaf axiom for $F$.

For any scheme $V$ and section $a\in F(V)$, the identity $D=U\times_XF$ gives $V\times_FD=V\times_XU$. The latter is a scheme surjective etale over $V$, by the scheme-test definition of the atlas $U\to X$. Consequently [lem-sfb-etale-sheaf-space-atlas-bootstrap], applied to the etale sheaf $F$ with scheme atlas $D$, makes $F$ an algebraic space $Z$. The closed-substack conclusion in step 3 says precisely that $Z\to X$ is representable by closed immersions. The map $D\to Z$ is surjective etale by the same scheme-test identity. A reduced scheme $D$ is reduced as an algebraic space because each of its etale scheme charts is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. The atlas $D\to Z$ is smooth on scheme charts by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Now [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality] implies that $Z$ is reduced. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the image of $D\to X$ equals that of $Z\to X$; it is $|p|(T_U)=T$.

source.place: Tag 0BH4 (lemma-spaces-etale-locally-representable); spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3 (lemma-reduced-local-smooth); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ, existence conclusion.

proof.text: If $Z_1\subset X$ is another reduced closed subspace with point image $T$, its pullback $D_1=U\times_XZ_1$ is a closed subscheme of $U$. It is an etale scheme chart of $Z_1$ by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], and hence is reduced by the stated definition of reduced algebraic space. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] its image in $U$ is $T_U$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives $D_1=D$. The injectivity of the bijection in [lem-sfb-invariant-closed-substack-descent] then gives $Z_1=Z$ as subfunctors of $X$. This supplies the uniqueness proof omitted in Tag 03IQ.

source.place: Tag 03IQ, last sentence (omitted uniqueness), filled using Tag 01J3 and stacks-properties.tex Tag 0507.

proof.text: Put $P=Z\times_XW$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and let $j:P\to W$ be the projection. For any scheme $V\to W$, associativity of compatible pairs identifies $P\times_WV=Z\times_XV$ over $V$. This is a scheme closed in $V$ because $Z\to X$ is a representable closed immersion. These are exactly the scheme tests for $j$ to be a closed immersion. No reducedness of $P$ is used.

source.place: Tag 02YW (lemma-base-change-immersions), closed case; formal scheme-test argument.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $\operatorname{im}|j|=|q|^{-1}(\operatorname{im}|i|)=|q|^{-1}(T)=:B$. Choose a scheme atlas $v:V\to W$, and put $P_V=P\times_WV$. Its map $j_V:P_V\to V$ is a closed immersion of schemes. To check injectivity of $|j|$, let $a,b\in|P|$ map to the same $w\in|W|$, and choose $u\in|V|$ above $w$. The point-surjectivity for fibre products in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives lifts of $(a,u)$ and $(b,u)$ to $|P_V|$. Since $|j_V|$ is injective by [def-weil-closed-immersion], the lifts coincide, so $a=b$. Thus $|j|$ is a continuous bijection onto $B$.

Let $C\subseteq|P|$ be closed. Its inverse image $C_V\subseteq|P_V|$ is closed, since the projection is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The scheme closed immersion $j_V$ sends $C_V$ to a closed subset of $V$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Point-surjectivity for the same fibre square gives $|v|^{-1}(|j|(C))=|j_V|(C_V)$. The map $|v|$ is an open continuous surjection by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. If a subset $H$ of $|W|$ has closed inverse image under $|v|$, its complement is $|v|(|v|^{-1}(H^c))$ and is open; thus $H$ is closed. Apply this to $H=|j|(C)$. Hence $|j|$ is closed, and the continuous bijection of step 7 has continuous inverse. It identifies $|P|$ homeomorphically with the subspace $B=|q|^{-1}(T)$, as required.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_reduced_closed_subspace {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Set (Point X.obj.obj)) (hT : IsClosed T) : ∃ C : ClosedSubspace X, IsReduced (C.val : AlgebraicSpace S) ∧ pointImage C.val.arrow.hom.hom = T ∧ (∀ D : ClosedSubspace X, IsReduced (D.val : AlgebraicSpace S) → pointImage D.val.arrow.hom.hom = T → D = C) ∧ ∀ (W : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : W ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (Limits.pullback.snd C.val.arrow.hom q.hom).hom ∧ ∃ e : Point (Limits.pullback C.val.arrow.hom q.hom).obj ≃ₜ {w : Point W.obj.obj | mapPoint q.hom.hom w ∈ T}, ∀ z : Point (Limits.pullback C.val.arrow.hom q.hom).obj, (e z).val = mapPoint (Limits.pullback.snd C.val.arrow.hom q.hom).hom z

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match: reduced closed subspace C exists with pointImage = T; uniqueness ranges over all reduced closed subspaces and gives subobject equality; for every q : W ⟶ X the sheaf-pullback projection is representable by closed immersions; the pullback's points are homeomorphic to {w | mapPoint q w ∈ T}, pinned to the projection's own mapPoint; no reducedness is asserted for the base change. The three added landed stmt_deps (closed subspace, reduced space, proper-curve-moduli as owner of mapPoint) create no cycle; mapPoint is the only map on points in the project's Lean trees.
